statement: Full-text search is a rebuildable retrieval index, not evidence authority.
actakit_implication: Treat FTS as projection/index that can be rebuilt from canonical text/claims.

statement: SQLite can enforce a stricter relational baseline than loose dynamic typing suggests.
actakit_implication: Use explicit columns/FKs/constraints; reserve JSON for versioned extensible payloads such as locators.

statement: WAL is same-machine only, permits one writer and can grow under long readers/checkpoint starvation.
actakit_implication: Use local attached storage, one canonical writer path, short transactions/read snapshots and explicit checkpoint monitoring.

statement: Foreign-key enforcement must be explicitly enabled on each SQLite connection.
actakit_implication: Connection bootstrap must set/verify required PRAGMAs before any canonical read/write service starts.

statement: A live SQLite database requires the backup API or equivalent consistent snapshot mechanism rather than naive file copying.
actakit_implication: Backup/restore design is part of storage correctness, not an afterthought.

statement: Recent SQLite releases have fixed WAL/concurrency corruption and deadlock defects.
actakit_implication: Declare/test a minimum SQLite version and include upstream defect history in upgrade policy.

statement: External/contentless FTS indexes can diverge from authoritative content unless maintained and checked.
actakit_implication: FTS stays rebuildable and integrity-checkable; never make it canonical evidence/claim storage.

statement: In STRICT tables, every PRIMARY KEY component is implicitly NOT NULL, so a nullable semantic field cannot also serve as a primary-key component.
actakit_implication: Use stable row identity or non-null keys for links whose role/mention fields are genuinely optional; do not encode optionality into a composite PRIMARY KEY.

statement: SQLite logical deletion does not by itself guarantee removal of recoverable prior content from the database file.
actakit_implication: A purge contract must include database-level scrubbing such as secure_delete/VACUUM semantics and must not equate DELETE with physical erasure.

statement: FTS5 deletion requires its own secure-delete behavior in addition to SQLite core secure_delete if old indexed terms must not remain recoverable.
actakit_implication: Purge must explicitly scrub FTS projections; ordinary FTS maintenance is insufficient for sensitive deletion.

statement: The WAL-reset corruption bug affects WAL builds through SQLite 3.51.2 and is fixed in 3.51.3 and later, making the runtime version floor part of durability rather than convenience.
actakit_implication: Treat 3.51.3 as the upstream WAL-fix boundary, not by itself as the final support-set rule; release withdrawal/maintenance status must also constrain the baseline.

statement: External-content FTS requires application-maintained consistency, while contentless variants trade away content access/rebuild behavior; a normal self-content FTS table can be the simpler disposable projection at canton scale.
actakit_implication: Prefer ordinary FTS5 projection tables rebuilt from canonical rows; pay small duplicate-text cost to reduce rowid coupling and projection-maintenance complexity.

statement: SQLite recursive CTE semantics distinguish UNION duplicate suppression from UNION ALL retention; the documented graph traversal uses UNION to prevent cycle repetition.
actakit_implication: Treat ClaimRelation as a multigraph: deduplicate node reachability while preserving edge identity in path/edge queries, with explicit depth/result bounds.

statement: A numeric minimum of 3.51.3 would admit withdrawn 3.52.0; the current 3.53 maintenance line is the clean initial support baseline for a new no-legacy deployment.
actakit_implication: Set the initial candidate floor to SQLite 3.53.4, the current stable maintenance release at review time; certify the exact packaged runtime/source ID and required compile options rather than relying only on numeric comparison.
